item.title: AI is becoming the new engine of climate risk assessment – should we be worried?
item.description: Are organisations ready for the governance, accountability and strategic implications that come with handing climate analysis to algorithms?

item.title: Juan Miguel Cuna appointed as Philippines’ acting environment secretary
item.description: Cuna replaces Raphael Lotilla, as the outgoing environment chief is designated to be the country's ambassador to the Vatican.

item.title: Australia spends $18 billion more harming nature than protecting it, study finds
item.description: A new study finds Australia spends far more on subsidies that harm biodiversity than on conservation, underscoring the need to reform fiscal policy to meet its 2030 global nature targets.

item.title: Rethinking coal phase-out in Asia and beyond
item.description: To accelerate the retirement of coal, we need a scalable incentive framework that offers equitable participation and fair distribution of costs and benefits.

item.title: Asia leads global shift toward sustainable investing, survey finds
item.description: Nearly four in five regional asset owners integrate sustainability factors, outpacing Europe and North America as climate risks and supportive policies drive adoption, acccording to FTSE Russell survey.

item.title: Malaysia to integrate water pricing into national adaptation plan, says environment ministry
item.description: The impacts of deforestation must also be counted towards the true cost of water, the ministry’s secretary-general said. The country's first fair share carbon budget report could help strengthen the government’s forest conservation efforts.

item.title: Thailand's decarbonisation ambition deserves a bond to match
item.description: As Asean's government to issue a sustainability-linked bond, Thailand could innovate further by linking fixed income instruments to decarbonisation using "transition linkers". Yet this must be matched by policy credibility.

item.title: Global plastic demands could more than double by 2050 despite harm evidence: study
item.description: The plastics boom is being driven by fossil fuel and petrochemical giants banking on rising production of packaging, including for ready meals, found a new Greenpeace report.

item.title: Asia Pacific insurers warn climate shocks are becoming a systemic financial threat
item.description: Insurance companies increasingly worry that escalating climate extremes could destabilise financial systems, not their balance sheets – an anxiety felt acutely in Asia Pacific, a MSCI study finds.

item.title: South Korea, Singapore sign pact to study small modular reactors
item.description: Deal marks first nuclear MOU between KHNP and Singapore agency as city-state explores low-carbon power options.
